Expected deaths from draws and future exposures

Source: R/model-draws.R
mt_deaths.Rd

Multiplies rate draws by exposures and optionally adds Poisson noise, so that the result describes observable death counts.

Usage

mt_deaths(draws, exposure = NULL, noise = TRUE, seed = NULL)

Arguments

draws

An mt_draws object.

exposure

Future exposures: an mt_data object with exposures (for example a population projection converted with mt_as_exposure()), or an array [age, period, stratum] or matrix [age, stratum] (used for every period) with dimnames, as mt_array() returns. Ages, years and strata are matched by their labels. Default: the exposures of the last training year.

noise

Add Poisson noise (draws of expected rates only; ignored for predictive draws, which contain it).

seed

Random seed.

Value

An array [age, period, stratum, draw] of deaths.

Details

Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) already contain the variation of the observed deaths (Poisson given the rates, or negative binomial for stanmomo(family = "nb")): for them no noise is added, whatever noise, and the result is their deaths. Give the exposures that were used for the forecast (its exposure); other exposures rescale the deaths and the result is then not a count.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(rwd(), x), h = 2, n_draws = 20, seed = 1)
dim(mt_deaths(fc))
#> [1] 71  2  2 20
